description: Experimental (the owner, 2026-11-06): Foxconn T99W640 / Dell DW5934e (Snapdragon X72) over USB, its MBIM composition 05c6:90d5 with cdc_mbim on interface 02 (dw5934e-5g-toolkit: USB\VID_05C6&PID_90D5&MI_02; 4PDA 1125602, kniga043 20.10.26: DIAG + ADB + MBIM). On USB it runs stably only when it powered up with PCIe connected and the PCIe bus was then cut physically (4PDA 1125602, Kilm 05.11.26); with PCIe left on it falls to no network until a reboot. The module is made for PCIe M.2 (MHI 105b:e11d eSIM, 105b:e11e, 105b:e118) and needs an M.2-to-USB adapter (4PDA 1125602, its first post: not USB out of the box). The ID is shared with the T99W175 in MBIM and the Compal RXM-G1: this profile takes it only by ModemManager's model (DMS over MBIM gives DP25-42843-47; a generic MBIM name leaves it to the T99W175 profile). Known faults, none curable from the router: a false PA temperature (sdr0_pa 131-137 °C at 34 °C) trips the modem's own thermal protection, which deregisters it and puts the radio to power save (powered, registration idle, no signal; persists across cold boots, a firmware fault: the toolkit's OEM fix request); a deadlock after a foreign base station's reject, held off by a periodic ping (4PDA 1125602 #59; the engine's reach checks send traffic anyway). So ModemManager alone, no AT, no driver rebind or USB re-authorize (a runtime driver switch killed the device in the toolkit's notes), recovery only on the operator's request, a long settle for the X72's boot. Reference: docs/modem-zoo/modems/foxconn-t99w640.md, observations F32, F33 Further firmware-specific read-only commands and the separate QMI-over-MBIM AT, FTM and DIAG paths are documented in docs/modem-zoo/modems/foxconn-t99w640-at-diag.md. This is reference-only: no firmware writes or automatic AT/DIAG polling, no native vendor AT-over-MBIM implementation.

hints.title: Dell DW5934e / T99W640 (X72)

firmware_research.source_revision: user research v2.4 / 2026-11-18; ENG read-only live tests and Retail static analysis; not verified against a working MedveModem router
firmware_research.cpu: Qualcomm SDX72; separate AP atfwd-daemon and CP Hexagon
firmware_research.api_status: reference-only: no generic native AT-over-MBIM/QCDM implementation or automatic AT reads

at_transport.pcie_mbim: /dev/wwan0mbim0: vendor QMI-over-MBIM AT path; firmware private Foxconn 0xE3 / 0x555D TLV 0x10; unsupported
at_transport.pcie_serial: /dev/wwan0at0: may not work on Retail (missing mhi_pipe_32)
at_transport.usb_serial: /dev/ttyUSB2: if actually enumerated; no assumption that 05c6:90d5 provides it
at_transport.diag: /dev/wwan0qcdm0 or /dev/ttyUSB0; QCDM not enabled by MedveModem

semantics.lte_lock: Read AT+LTE_LOCK? only; WRITE form AT+LTE_LOCK=<PCI>,<EARFCN>[,<PCI>,<EARFCN>...] (PCI first), up to eight pairs, not enabled; bare AT+LTE_LOCK clears lock
semantics.band_mode: AT+SLMODE=<term 0 transient|1 NV>,<pref_mode 0..7>; enum differs from SDX55 bit mask
semantics.ca: AT+CA_ENABLE=0 enables CA; 1..255 disables, never write from telemetry
semantics.rssi: AT+RSSI=LTE,ALL reports antenna measurements; AT+RSSI? alone can fail
semantics.fcc: AT+FCC_LOCK? may omit OK; changing FCC NV flag is not authenticated host QMI FCC unlock

firmware_research.dangerous_side_effects: Do not add bare commands as read probes: AT+ODIS resets ODIS, bare LTE_LOCK clears lock, bare ULCA removes feature-disable flag; some AT+CMD=? calls are unsupported; do not execute dangerous/FTM/DIAG in production

ftm.via: vendor QMI text dispatcher, commands lack AT prefix

warnings: Firmware ENG read-only probes are not proof of availability or safety on Retail; do not run any AT while ModemManager owns the device
On ENG AT+VZWRSRP? and AT+VZWRSRQ? crash CP (MHI SSR). Avoid even as reads; use AT$QCSQ or AT$QCRSRP where an exclusive supported transport exists
AT+ODIS without ? performs factory reset; bare AT+LTE_LOCK clears cell lock; bare AT+ULCA mutates EFS
FCC_LOCK=0 and ftm unlock_fcc are NOT the host's authenticated QMI FCC unlock
No automatic writes to RFNV/EFS, DIAG, FTM, USB compositions, SAR power configuration or identity

recovery.source: experimental: reconnect, radio and reset through ModemManager on the operator's request only; no rebind or re-authorize (toolkit: a runtime driver switch gave «Device died»); the thermal fault is not cured by any reset; T99W640 firmware reference v2.4 (2026-11-18) confirms native PCIe AT can be absent on Retail and contains dangerous AT/DIAG/FTM traps; neither owner nor recovery policy changed
